results.title: Taxing the Digital Ledger: Platform Labour and Fiscal Invisibility
results.summary: How algorithmic dispatch, rating heuristics, and cloud data centre tax concessions render African women workers invisible in public revenue systems.
results.description: Led by Dr. Lyla Latif (Managing Partner Lai & Latif, Lecturer UoN Law, Chair Committee on Fiscal Studies, NED Tax Justice Network), this investigation pairs empirical tax law with civic oversight to interrogate platform worker classification.

author.name: Dr. Lyla Latif
author.role: Managing Partner Lai & Latif | Lecturer @UoNLawFaculty | Chair @CFS_UoN | NED @TaxJusticeNet

slides.text: Behind every ride-hailing ride, grocery delivery, and home care task, African women power the platform economy.
Platforms classify domestic cleaners and service workers as 'independent users', avoiding employer tax withholding and social insurance contributions.
Corporate income tax paid by hyperscale data centers operating under extended 10-year capital import and energy tax holiday concessions.
Through proactive regulatory sandboxes, Budget Ndio Story and House of Fiscal Wisdom test rules to make platform workers visible in the fiscal ledger.

results.title: Where your tax shilling goes
results.summary: A short scroll through how PAYE and VAT feed the national budget  --  and what counties receive.
results.description: A short scroll through how PAYE and VAT feed the national budget  --  and what counties receive.

slides.text: Every PAYE deduction is a claim on tomorrow’s classrooms, clinics, and roads.
National government keeps some revenue; counties get a share via the Division of Revenue.
County governments typically receive around this share of nationally raised revenue after equitable allocation.
